name: Stack overflow (infinite recursion / excessive call depth)
message: Infinite recursion or excessive call depth. The faulting frame is the symptom site, not the cause; look for repeating frames in the native stack.
fix: Identify the repeating call chain. If a mod's frames repeat, disable that mod.

name: Heap corruption
message: Heap corruption detected. The real culprit corrupted memory earlier in the session; the crash address is only where it was noticed, so the faulting module is not the suspect.
fix: Bisect mods that touch native code or memory. Check the breadcrumb tail and the loaded-mod set for recently-active mods.

name: Stack buffer overrun (/GS check failed)
message: A stack buffer overrun tripped the /GS security cookie. The offending function is in the frames near the faulting address.
fix: Identify the module owning the frames near the fault. If it is a mod, disable it.

name: In-page error (backing store read failed)
message: A memory page failed to load from its backing store. Possible causes: a bad disk sector, a disconnected drive, or a corrupted memory-mapped file.
fix: Verify game file integrity, check the drive the game is installed on, and retry after a clean reboot.

name: GPU device removed/reset (TDR)
message: The GPU was removed or reset (a Timeout Detection and Recovery event). This is a driver/hardware/overclock crash, not a mod.
fix: Clean-install the GPU drivers, revert any GPU overclock, and check thermals and power delivery.

name: Crash inside a DLSS / FSR / XeSS upscaler or frame-gen DLL
message: The crash faulted inside an upscaler / frame-generation DLL (DLSS, DLSS-G Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, FSR, or XeSS). That is the GPU render pipeline, not a mod - though a mod that pushes the GPU harder (heavy textures, extra effects) can make it fire more often. The live render settings and GPU driver are shown in this report.
fix: Toggle DLSS / Frame Generation / Ray Reconstruction off, lower the internal resolution, cap the framerate, and update or roll back the GPU driver. If it only happens with certain mods loaded, test those - recurrence and co-occurring mods are shown when this crash repeats.

name: Crash inside the GPU usermode driver
message: The crash faulted inside the GPU usermode driver - the rasterizer (nvwgf2umx/nvd3dumx), the ray-tracing driver (nvrtum64), or the shader compiler (nvgpucomp64). This is a driver/hardware crash, not a mod - though heavy GPU content (path tracing, ray reconstruction, 4K textures) can trigger it more often. The GPU driver version and live render settings are shown in this report.
fix: Clean-reinstall the current GPU driver (use DDU for a full wipe) and clear the shader cache. In-game, turn off Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction (the heaviest ray-tracing paths) and Frame Generation to test, and revert any GPU overclock/undervolt. If a clean reinstall does not resolve it, try a different driver version. If it only happens with certain mods loaded, those mods are stressing the driver, not corrupting it.

name: VRAM exhaustion at crash
message: Video memory was at or near its budget when the crash fired. This is a VRAM exhaustion crash; the most likely cause is texture-heavy content the GPU cannot hold.
fix: Lower the in-game texture quality, reduce 4K/8K texture mods, and check that no other GPU-heavy app is running.

name: Process commit exhaustion at crash
message: System committed memory was at or near its limit when the crash fired. Either the modlist is too memory-heavy for the available RAM + pagefile, or another app is consuming committed memory.
fix: Reduce the modlist's memory footprint (especially archive-heavy or scripted-heavy mods), close background apps, and check the system pagefile size.

name: Out of memory / VRAM exhaustion suspected
message: Memory or VRAM was near-exhausted at crash time. This is an environmental out-of-memory condition, not necessarily a specific mod.
fix: Lower texture and streaming settings, reduce the modlist's memory footprint, and check available system RAM and VRAM headroom.

name: ICU text-formatter crash on a scripted thread
message: The crash faulted inside the ICU Unicode text formatter while a scripted call was in flight. Almost always a buffer-overrun caused by a custom field on a vanilla data class that a scripted handler then asks vanilla code to format (e.g. a mod adds float values to a record where vanilla expects none, then a tooltip path tries to format them).
fix: Investigate the innermost scripted frame and the mod whose package the script is touching. If a recently-added mod started feeding custom fields into vanilla records, that is the lead.

name: Crash on item hover / tooltip resolution
message: The crash fired on the item-hover/tooltip surface. Most common causes: a broken TweakDB record lookup, a missing ResourcePath/icon CName, a NULL itemRecord dereference, or a mod adding fields to a record that vanilla cannot format.
fix: Open inventory and hover items one category at a time to narrow the offending item. Disable mods that touch item TweakDB records or tooltip injectors.

name: Crash during engine initialization
message: The crash fired while the engine was still initializing - before gameplay started. Init-time crashes are caused by mod load order or broken plugin DLLs, not by gameplay state.
fix: Bisect the load order: disable the bottom half of the mod list, then narrow. Check red4ext.log and the CET load log for plugin-load failures around the crash time.

name: Game freeze / hang (no exception)
message: The game stopped responding without an exception - a freeze/deadlock, detected by REDscope's watchdog after no scripted activity for the timeout window. A hang produces no fault, so there is no faulting address; the scripted functions that were last running (the leads) are where to look.
fix: If a specific mod's scripted function is named below and recurs across multiple hangs, disable that mod. Freezes during streaming or loading can also be environmental (disk stalls, GPU driver hangs).

name: A required framework is not loaded
message: Installed mods need a framework (Cyber Engine Tweaks or TweakXL) that is not loaded. Those mods do nothing and the mismatch can crash the game - common after a game update that breaks a framework. This is a setup problem, not a specific mod's fault.
fix: Reinstall or update the named framework and confirm it loads (check the red4ext and CET logs at startup). See the setupIntegrity section for which framework is missing.
